_meta.purpose: The five events the site is allowed to record. Defined in this session because no definition existed in the repo (FLG-006, SG-12).

universal_fields.ts: ISO-8601 UTC, second precision, set by the collector on arrival - never trusted from the client
universal_fields.ev: one of the event ids below
universal_fields.path: site-relative pathname of the page that fired the event
universal_fields.sid: random per-page-load id, discarded when the tab closes; not a cookie, not persistent

hard_rules: No event may be fired by an automated process. Generating clicks or impressions artificially, by robot or software, is prohibited by the Participation Requirements [S12].
The collector must not store or log the source IP address [S19]; it does not.
No cross-page identity stitching: sid is per page load, so 'sessions' here are not users.
A sub-tag or report identifier must never be tied to a specific visitor [S03]. The collector therefore never forwards anything to Amazon.

events.name: page_view
events.fires_on: the page's own script, after first paint, once per load
events.answers: Did anyone arrive, and on which page?
events.not_recorded: referrer string, user agent, screen size, IP
events.why_limited: Referrer is deliberately dropped: it is the only field in this design that could identify a person's browsing, and the value of keeping it is smaller than the cost of disclosing it.

events.name: guide_view
events.fires_on: a guide or topic page, when the reader has been visible to the page for 30 seconds or has scrolled past 75%, whichever comes first
events.answers: Is the editorial work being read, or bounced from?
events.not_recorded: mouse movement, keystrokes, exact scroll trace
events.why_limited: A threshold instead of a continuous trace keeps it a reading signal rather than surveillance, and 'engaged' means something defensible: 30 seconds is stated in the schema, so it cannot quietly be redefined later to flatter a page.

events.name: outbound_click
events.fires_on: pointer activation on an element marked data-affiliate, before navigation
events.answers: Which shelf card or which paragraph turned a reader into a click - the only on-site signal that has a commission attached to it.
events.not_recorded: the final URL, the query string, anything after the host
events.why_limited: tag_present is a boolean, not the tag value, so the event never carries account credentials anywhere they do not belong. Nothing is sent to Amazon; the click itself is what Amazon measures, and its report is the only conversion source we trust [S18].

events.name: disclosure_view
events.fires_on: the disclosure strip entering the viewport on a page that contains at least one outbound link (IntersectionObserver; no timer, no synthetic firing)
events.answers: Does the disclosure actually appear before the click, which is the claim the site makes about itself?
events.not_recorded: whether the reader read it - nobody can measure that honestly
events.why_limited: This is a placement instrument, not a legal defence. Seeing a strip is not comprehension, and no report should ever claim that the ratio above satisfies the FTC standard on its own.

events.name: product_intent_confirmation
events.fires_on: the local collector, when tools/product_intake.py confirm writes a confirmation record (so the shelf's go-live trail is time-stamped by a server, not by an editor's claim)
events.answers: When did a product become shoppable, on what evidence, and who said so?
events.not_recorded: nothing extra is needed; the durable copy is the git commit of data/products.json
events.why_limited: The register is the truth; this event is only its clock. Do not treat it as proof of a buyer's consent or of the listing's accuracy.
